extracted.intended_audience: professional photographers (photojournalists/documentary photographers) intending to enter the World Press Photo 2026 Contest
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation/eligibility criteria for submitting photographs to the World Press Photo 2026 Contest, covering who may enter, technical and ethical standards, manipulation/AI limits, submission process, and legal/usage terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and balanced selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Being a global platform means a responsibility to present the most accurate and compelling work – presenting a balanced selection of stories from around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World Press Photo applies the entry rules and recruits a highly qualified and diverse jury to facilitate a fair entry and judging process. Entrants should expect judges to evaluate accuracy and balance as part of contest selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant agreement to entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Every entrant must read these entry rules and agree to them when submitting their entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry rules outline who can enter the contest and what can be entered; agreeing to them is mandatory to enter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional status eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest is open to professional photographers working in the field of journalism and/or documentary photography. Every entrant must provide a document with a valid date that confirms their current professional status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable documents include a press card, at least one proof of publication from 2024 or 2025 (with name visible as credit), journalism union membership card, membership document from a recognized photographic association showing professional membership, or a recent (2024 or 2025) letter of reference from a photo agency, photo editor, media organisation or publication. If unable to provide these, entrants may register with alternative multiple documents to clarify professional status. Not accepted as proof: CVs or cover letters, diplomas, or samples of photography. The organisation may request additional information to clarify status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team entry proof requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Team entries of two or more photographers are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of professional status must be provided for each team member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The photographer(s) must be the author(s) of the photographs submitted in their name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must only submit work they created.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright authority to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: The photographer(s), agent or representative entering on their behalf, must be the copyright holder(s) or have been authorized by the copyright holder(s) to submit the photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions require either copyright ownership or explicit authorization from the copyright owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must comply with the categories, as described on the contest's categories page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should check the categories page for definitions, eligible formats and category-specific rules before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical requirements compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must meet the technical requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the contest's technical requirements page for file formats, size/resolution, naming conventions and other technical specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published or unpublished images allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs can be submitted whether or not they have been published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication does not preclude entry unless other rules (e.g., category-specific) prohibit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restricted-event photography
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs taken at restricted events are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricted events are those where only photographers commissioned by organisers have access (for example photographers commissioned by governments, political parties or corporations). Such images are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions and descriptions in English
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries must have accurate captions and descriptions, written in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If captions have been translated, provide the original caption as well. Captions must contain all the information described in the guidance on captions (see linked guidance). Accurate, complete captions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry must include relevant additional information such as motivation, the type of project (assignment/personal project) and funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context about why and how the work was produced and any funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with code of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries must comply with the World Press Photo code of ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and follow the code of ethics (linked). Ethical breaches can lead to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official submission platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries can only be submitted via Picter, the official contest entry platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions via other platforms or email will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for creating an account, completing registration and submitting entries to the 2026 Contest is 17 January 2026, 13.00 Central European Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All steps (account creation, registration, submission) must be completed by this deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest / staff and jury ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the World Press Photo staff, Supervisory Board, International Advisory Committee and 2026 Contest jury are not permitted to enter the 2026 Contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees and specified officials must not submit entries to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-use of photographs across entry types
rubrics_metrics.description: A photograph can only be entered once, either as a Single or as part of a Story, or as part of a Long-Term Project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same image in multiple categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: No visible credits or identifying marks on images
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs must not show the name of the photographer, agency, or publication, or any other information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These details can be included in the metadata of the photograph but must not be visible on the photograph itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation prohibition for Singles/Stories/Long-Term Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: All photographs entered to the contest must comply with our rules on manipulation and must not be altered by adding, rearranging, reversing, distorting or removing people and/or objects from within the frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the linked rules on manipulation for full details and examples. Manipulating content to change the scene or subjects is forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of original camera files for finalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must provide file(s) as recorded by the camera for all images that proceed to the final stages of the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These files will be requested and studied confidentially between 26 January and 22 February 2026. Failure to provide them when requested will lead to exclusion of the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: AI-generated images are not photography
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated images are not photography. A photograph captures light on a sensor or film; it is a record of a physical moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle underpins the contest's restrictions on synthetic or artificially generated imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-capture requirement (no synthetic images)
rubrics_metrics.description: All photographs entered into the contest must be made with a camera. No synthetic or artificially generated images are allowed, and no use of artificially generative fill is allowed in post-production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any use of synthetic or generative image creation or fill will automatically disqualify the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smartphone mode restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Smartphone photographs are permitted only when captured in standard shooting mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions created using HDR, portrait mode, creative lighting effects, or panorama mode are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited use of AI-powered enhancement tools permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of smart tools, or AI-powered enhancement tools is possible within the contest rules, as long as these tools do not lead to significant changes to the image as a whole, introduce new information to the image, nor remove information from the image that was captured by the camera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of tools where limited usage may be allowed: denoise, automatic adjustments (levels, colors, contrast) and object selection for local adjustments. These are permitted only to the extent that they do not alter, add or remove information captured by the camera. Determinations are made by the contest organisation and global jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited AI-powered enlarging/sharpening tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools that immediately breach the contest rules and are not allowed are all AI powered enlarging tools such as Adobe Super Resolution and Topaz Photo AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools are based on generative AI models that introduce new information to enlarge and sharpen images and are therefore disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright grant for awarded entries
rubrics_metrics.description: For awarded entries, copyright holders grant World Press Photo unlimited non-exclusive use of high-resolution photographs for activities in all media, including social media, online and print, in relation to the contest, the exhibition, the yearbook, the public archive, and all promotional and educational activities for and under the auspices of World Press Photo, without any remuneration being due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award winners should expect World Press Photo to use high-resolution images broadly for contest-related activities without payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright grant for non-awarded entries
rubrics_metrics.description: For all entries except awarded entries, copyright holders grant World Press Photo non-exclusive use of low-resolution photographs in a non-public archive for its educational and research activities, without any remuneration being due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-awarded entrants permit low-res use for internal/educational/research purposes without payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warranties and indemnification by copyright holders
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyright holders represent and warrant that submission of the entries does not breach any law, and further that no third party can hold any claims or any objections regarding the rights granted to World Press Photo specified in articles 21 and 22. The copyright holders will hold World Press Photo harmless of any claims from third parties related hereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must ensure they have rights to submit and license images as described and accept liability for third-party claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Entry Rules and any dispute, proceedings or claim of whatever nature arising out of or in any way relating to the Entry Rules (including any non-contractual disputes or claims), shall be governed by Dutch law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants agree Dutch law governs interpretation and disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute arising from the Entry Rules (whether contractual or non-contractual) shall be decided solely and exclusively by the competent court of Amsterdam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants accept Amsterdam courts as the exclusive forum for disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisation's discretion to refuse or exclude entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The conditions set out in the Entry Rules are binding, and World Press Photo reserves the right to refuse or exclude any entry at its own discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World Press Photo can refuse or exclude entries even where other rules are satisfied; decisions rest with the organisation.
